group.passage:
While space exploration represents a remarkable scientific milestone, it also exposes astronauts to a range of serious health risks. [[1]] stays in space result in physiological changes similar to the natural aging process on Earth. Among the most significant challenges is bone density loss, as the absence of gravity reduces mechanical stress on the skeleton. Astronauts also suffer from muscle atrophy, where muscles weaken due to less physical demand on them. [[2]], their bones become more fragile because they receive less stress from weakened muscles, increasing the risk of fractures upon their return.
Another critical concern involves the immune system. Research has demonstrated lower white blood cell production, which leaves astronauts more [[3]] infections. Additionally, factors such as radiation exposure, isolation, and disruption of the body’s natural schedule may speed up the aging process. Experts have noted that spaceflight can impact telomeres, the protectors at the ends of DNA strands.
Re-adapting to Earth’s gravity presents [[4]] another hurdle, and astronauts experience difficulties with fundamental activities such as walking, balancing, and standing, as their bodies readjust. [[5]] these matters, space agencies continue to research countermeasures, including specialized exercise routines, nutritional support, and medical interventions, in the hope of safeguarding astronaut health on future space expeditions.

tags.topic: health risks of long stays in space for astronauts
